title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ（田中基嗣研究室）
subtitle: Design Project III(Tanaka Mototsugu)
teachers:
TANAKA Mototsugu
授業科目の学習・教育目標
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) Acquire the ability to identify and solve problems to research, develop, design, and manufacture socially useful and high-quality products using the basic knowledge learned in the Department of Mechanical Engineering.
(2) Learn what technologies or new mechanisms are needed for that purpose.
(3) Learn about the importance of collaboration with society (particularly local communities).
advice:
This is the final comprehensive course in the Department of Mechanical Engineering. To realize the educational objectives of the Department of Mechanical Engineering, this course focuses on the following goals:
Students will acquire the ability to model phenomena accurately and analyze the models.
Students will acquire the ability and the engineering sense to evaluate solutions based on the obtained results.
In practice, students should reconfirm their project theme, which was determined in Preparatory Seminar, with the supervisors of the individual laboratories. (The theme should be revised as necessary.)
Students are expected to pursue the identification and solution of problems in accordance with the engineering process.
This laboratory focuses on the advanced composite materials. In addition, we also investigate approaches to apply conventional advanced technologies and knowledge to composite materials for other fields, such as the global environment, regenerative medicine, cellular biomechanics, tissue engineering, and biomimetics. The new results obtained by these trials provide feedback to many fields, such as mechanical and aeronautical engineering. Thus, we aim to cultivate flexible and comprehensive thinking abilities regardless of the academic field.

achievementLevels.ideal:
(1) Understand the purpose of your project and the advancement process accurately, and achieve the established annual goal. The process can be reported in the Design Project Activity Support System.
(2) Compile and present the intermediate results for the project into the interim report. Complete the final report, present it to the Design Project III Public Presentation Review Board.
(3) If necessary, design and manufacture your own experimental devices, and also evaluate the performance of the product. (The numbers in the text correspond to those of the student’s action goals.)
achievementLevels.standard:
(1) Understand the purpose of your project theme and the advancement process, and achieve the established annual goal. In addition, the process can be reported in the Design Project Activity Support System.
(2) Compile intermediate results for the project into the interim report, and present its content. Complete the final report and present it to the Design Project III Public Presentation Review Board.
(3) Design and manufacture your own experimental devices if necessary. (The numbers in the text correspond to those of the student’s action goals.)

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              This is the final comprehensive course in the Department of Mechanical Engineering. To realize the educational objectives of the Department of Mechanical Engineering, this course focuses on the following goals:
Students will acquire the ability to model phenomena accurately and analyze the models.
Students will acquire the ability and the engineering sense to evaluate solutions based on the obtained results.
In practice, students should reconfirm their project theme, which was determined in Preparatory Seminar, with the supervisors of the individual laboratories. (The theme should be revised as necessary.)
Students are expected to pursue the identification and solution of problems in accordance with the engineering process.
This laboratory focuses on the advanced composite materials. In addition, we also investigate approaches to apply conventional advanced technologies and knowledge to composite materials for other fields, such as the global environment, regenerative medicine, cellular biomechanics, tissue engineering, and biomimetics. The new results obtained by these trials provide feedback to many fields, such as mechanical and aeronautical engineering. Thus, we aim to cultivate flexible and comprehensive thinking abilities regardless of the academic field.
